3．論文への挿入用 LaTeX

最も簡単な二例に絞れば，次の記述で十分だと思います．原稿で定義されている exa 環境とマクロに合わせています．

\begin{exa}[The flatness hypothesis]\label{exa:nonflat}
The flatness hypothesis in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1}
cannot be omitted.
Let $R$ be a complete DVR of characteristic zero, with
uniformizer $\pi$ and residue field $k$, and set
\[
  A=R,\qquad I=\pi R,\qquad B=k[x].
\]
The $R$-algebra structure on $B$ is induced by $R\to k$.
Since
\[
  B\simeq R\{x\}/\pi R\{x\},
\]
the algebra $B$ is of henselian finite presentation over $R$.
Moreover, $IB=0$, so $(B,IB)$ is a henselian pair.
At the closed point $\fp=(\pi)$, we have
\[
  B\otimes_R\ka(\fp)\simeq k[x],
  \qquad
  \dim(B\otimes_R\ka(\fp))=1.
\]
However, $B$ is not $R$-flat, since $\pi B=0$ and $B\ne0$.
Finally,
\[
  X=\Sph(B,IB)=\Spec k[x]
\]
as locally ringed spaces, and hence
\[
  \HH^q(X,\cO_X)=0\qquad(q>0)
\]
by the usual vanishing theorem for quasi-coherent sheaves
on affine schemes
\cite[\tagref{01XB}]{stacks-project}.
\end{exa}

\begin{exa}[Zero-dimensional fibers]\label{exa:zero-dimensional}
The positive-dimensional fiber hypothesis in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} cannot be omitted either.
Let $R$ be a complete DVR of characteristic zero, with
uniformizer $\pi$, and take
\[
  A=B=R,\qquad I=\pi R,
\]
with the identity map $A\to B$.
Then $B$ is $A$-flat and of henselian finite presentation.
For every $\fp\in\Spec A$, we have
\[
  B\otimes_A\ka(\fp)\simeq\ka(\fp),
\]
so every fiber is nonempty and zero-dimensional.
On the other hand, the underlying topological space of
$X=\Sph(R,\pi R)$ consists of a single point.
The global sections functor on abelian sheaves on $X$
is therefore exact, and consequently
\[
  \HH^q(X,\cO_X)=0\qquad(q>0).
\]
\end{exa}

この二例を並べれば，平坦性を外すと，正次元の特殊ファイバーがあっても消滅し得ることと，平坦であっても，正次元ファイバーの存在を仮定しなければ非消滅は保証されないことを，それぞれ独立に示せます．
